articles.title: Indian investors bullish on AI stocks amid volatility
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Indian retail investors who piled into Nvidia shares during the recent US technology stock rout are largely holding on to their investments,
articles.body: BENGALURU: Indian retail investors who piled into Nvidia shares during the recent US technology stock rout are largely holding on to their investments, with some buying more even as the chipmaker’s shares surged 31% on Monday following the return of founder Jensen Huang as chief executive.Fewer than 3% of investors who bought Nvidia during the correction on INDmoney sold any of their shares on Monday, while one in eight bought more, data shared with TOI showed. More than nine in ten investors who bought the stock after the Nov 12 selloff are now in profit, with average gains of over 10%.Monday was Nvidia’s biggest trading day on INDmoney by value, with the stock accounting for 28% of all US stock trading on the platform. On Vested, the stock accounted for 22% of total traded value. On both platforms, buying accounted for 74% of Nvidia’s traded value.“Indian investors are increasingly treating global AI leaders the way they treat India’s blue-chips: a sharp correction is a chance to build a position, not a reason to run,” said Ashish Kashyap, founder and chief executive of INDmoney.Between early Oct and Nov 23, the number of Nvidia shares held by INDmoney investors rose 39%. On Vested, 84% of Monday’s Nvidia buyers had previously bought the stock, while the rest were first-time buyers.On Groww, orders for Nvidia shares rose more than 15-fold between the beginning of November and Friday. On Nov 9, when Nvidia was among the biggest losers on Wall Street, orders more than tripled from the previous session.“What stands out is how Indian investors are approaching AI. They are not picking one name. They are building exposure across the full AI value chain, from chips with Nvidia and Micron, to models with Anthropic, to platforms with Microsoft. Nvidia’s dip this month didn’t shake that conviction. In fact, buying picked up on the red days,” said Harsh Jain, co-founder and COO of Groww. Last week, Claude maker Anthropic accounted for 40% of orders on INDmoney on its market debut.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: RBI to widen market for government securities: DG Jain
articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI is seeking to broaden retail participation in govt securities (G-secs) and improve secondary-market liquidity by making it easier for
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI is seeking to broaden retail participation in govt securities (G-secs) and improve secondary-market liquidity by making it easier for individual investors to access the market and encouraging primary dealers (PDs) to expand their market-making activities.Speaking at Primary Dealers’ Association of India (PDAI) Seminar 2026 here on Monday, RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain outlined measures to widen the investor base and distribute trading activity more evenly across the yield curve at a time when there is a drop in demand from long-term institutional investors.“It has been observed that demand from banks, insurers and pension funds for long-term sovereign debt has marginally declined, with insurance and pension funds shifting towards more of equity exposure. This has structurally reduced such demand for govt securities,” said Jain.To widen the investor base, Jain said PDs could play a greater role by acting as active market makers under the scheme, conducting awareness campaigns and educating retail investors about the benefits of these instruments. They could also tailor bond offerings to retail investors, including shorter-tenor STRIPS (Separate Trading of Registered Interest and Principal of Securities), which are relatively easier to understand.To improve secondary-market liquidity, RBI has reduced the frequency of benchmark G-sec issuances and increased the volume offered in each auction. These measures have helped improve trading liquidity, but it remains lower than in other countries.Jain said PDs should increase market-making activity, particularly by providing two-way quotes in off-the-run securities.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Wall Street jitters: Nasdaq retreats after Nvidia-fuelled rally; Anthropic slips below IPO price
articles.summary: Wall Street retreated on Tuesday as technology stocks gave back some of the previous day's sharp gains, with investors booking profits and turning
articles.body: Wall Street retreated on Tuesday as technology stocks gave back some of the previous day's sharp gains, with investors booking profits and turning cautious ahead of key US inflation data. Nvidia and Anthropic led the decline in AI-linked stocks.The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54, while the S&P 500 declined 0.50% to 7,201.09. However, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70.The pullback came a day after Wall Street staged a strong rally, driven by Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO. The rebound, however, failed to ease concerns over stretched AI valuations, rising infrastructure spending and the outlook for interest rates.Anthropic falls below IPO priceAnthropic shares tumbled 6.5% to $81.90, slipping below their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83, just days after the AI startup's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.The stock opened at $111.50 on November 19, with its fully diluted valuation briefly exceeding $2 trillion. However, it has since lost ground amid a broader technology selloff.Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its IPO after underwriters exercised their option to purchase additional shares, making it the biggest public offering on record and surpassing SpaceX's $85.7 billion listing in June.CEO Dario Amodei sold more than 3.37 million shares worth over $280 million a day after the IPO, according to a filing late on Monday.The company's rapid reversal has renewed concerns about elevated AI valuations and the massive investments being made in computing infrastructure, particularly as higher interest rates could increase financing costs, Reuters reported.Anthropic is not the first major technology company to fall below its IPO price soon after listing. SpaceX took about a month to slip below its offer price, while Facebook, now Meta Platforms, fell below its IPO price on its second trading day in 2012.Nvidia, chip stocks retreat after rallyNvidia shares fell 5.9% as investors reassessed the implications of Jensen Huang's return as CEO and the political and governance risks surrounding the company.The chipmaker had surged nearly 30% on Monday after Huang's reinstatement, helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq post their biggest daily percentage gains since April 2025.Technology stocks led the declines on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 technology sector falling 2.8%. The semiconductor index dropped 7.9%, reflecting renewed selling in AI-linked companies.Before Monday's rally, AI stocks had struggled for weeks as investors questioned whether the sector's debt-fuelled spending on infrastructure would generate sufficient returns.Investors await US inflation data, tariff developmentsInvestors are also looking ahead to Wednesday's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation gauge watched by the Federal Reserve ahead of its December policy meeting.Persistent inflation has strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy. Fed funds futures traders were pricing in a 98% probability of a rate hike in December and a 66% chance of another increase in January, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said late on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point towards tighter monetary policy.Investors were also wary of potential new tariffs after Reuters reported, citing three people familiar with the matter, that the Trump administration was preparing to release findings of a probe into alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners. The findings are expected to pave the way for new import duties on a wide range of goods.The administration's tariffs have contributed to higher consumer prices in the US, adding to inflation concerns.Dollar slips, bond yields steadyThe dollar fell 0.44% against a basket of major currencies, retreating from a 20-month high touched earlier in the session.The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes edged up 0.77 basis points to 4.928%, compared with 4.92% late on Monday.The gap between two-year and 10-year Treasury yields, a closely watched indicator of economic expectations, stood at 24.3 basis points.Gold futures fell 2.67% and silver futures dropped 5.75%, pressured by hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials and expectations of higher interest rates.Brent crude futures settled $2.03 higher, or 2.27%, at $91.40 a barrel after a volatile session, with fresh attacks reported on vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Landlord earned Rs 2.73 crore as rent, filed ITR and slotted it as ‘Income from House Property’, but taxman reclassifies it as business income and raises taxable income to Rs 1.07 crore; why ITAT Surat gave relief
articles.summary: You earn rental income from commercial properties. When filing your income tax return, under what head can you classify it?
articles.body: You earn rental income from commercial properties. When filing your income tax return, under what head can you classify it?In one case, a landlord earned rent from and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head. However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) issued him a notice and classified the rental receipts as business income.What the case is aboutA landlord earned Rs 2.73 crore in rent from his commercial properties and reported the amount in his income tax return (ITR) under the “Income from House Property” head.However, the AO reclassified the rental receipts as business income. This pushed the landlord’s total taxable income up from the Rs 24.07 lakh that he had originally declared to Rs 1.07 crore.The sharp increase resulted from the change in the tax treatment of his rental earnings. Under the “Income from House Property” head, taxpayers can claim a flat standard deduction of 30% on the net annual value after deducting eligible municipal taxes paid.When rental receipts are assessed as business income, however, taxpayers can claim eligible business expenses incurred to earn that income. This difference in the deductions available explains why the landlord’s taxable income rose from Rs 24.07 lakh to Rs 1.07 crore.The landlord calculated that if his rental earnings of around Rs 2.7 crore were assessed as income from house property, he would be entitled to claim Rs 81.52 lakh as a standard deduction under Section 24, along with Rs 1.63 lakh for municipal taxes he had paid, according to an ET report on the judgement.By treating the rent as business income, the AO denied the landlord the benefit of the deductions available under the house-property head. The CIT (Appeals) subsequently upheld the AO’s decision.The landlord then challenged the order before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Surat. On November 4, 2026, he won on the key question of how his rental income should be classified for tax purposes.Why did ITAT Surat give relief to landlord?The landlord’s business involves dealing in land and constructing buildings. He earned rent from industrial buildings that formed part of his stock-in-trade, or business assets. The Assessing Officer relied on this aspect while assessing the rental receipts under the head “Income from Business or Profession”.The landlord, however, maintained that his business was the “business of dealing in lands and construction of buildings”, and not the “business of letting out buildings”.ITAT Surat held that the fact that he dealt in land, constructed buildings and rented out properties held as stock-in-trade for sale did not, by itself, settle the question of how the rental receipts should be classified. The determining factor was the nature of the activity from which the income arose.The tribunal referred to the Supreme Court’s ruling in Chennai Properties and Investments Ltd. (supra), in which rental income was treated as business income because letting out properties was itself the assessee’s business.However, ITAT Surat distinguished that ruling, along with the other judgments relied upon by the CIT (Appeals), on the ground that those cases involved taxpayers whose business was letting out properties.The tribunal also noted that the Gujarat High Court’s ruling in Commissioner of Income-tax v. New India Industries Ltd. (1993) 201 ITR 208 (Guj) supported the landlord’s contention that his rental earnings were taxable under the head “Income from House Property”.The tribunal further observed that the lower authorities had not recorded any finding that the landlord was engaged in the business of letting out properties. It also noted that no material had been placed before it to establish that he was carrying on such a business.Chartered Accountant Chintan Ghelani told ET that the landlord’s case succeeded because ITAT Surat distinguished between conducting a real-estate business and carrying on a business of letting out properties.Ghelani explained that rent earned from industrial buildings cannot automatically be classified as business income merely because those properties are held as stock-in-trade, or business assets.Under income tax law, rental earnings from letting out properties, including buildings, are ordinarily taxable as house-property income under Section 22. However, such receipts may be assessed as business income if the facts establish that letting out properties is itself the taxpayer’s business.In this case, ITAT Surat observed that the lower authorities had not recorded any finding that he was engaged in the business of letting out properties. Nor had any material been brought before the tribunal to establish that this was the nature of his business.Ghelani also pointed out that Section 23(5) expressly recognises that a property forming part of stock-in-trade can still come within the scope of the house-property provisions. Therefore, while the classification of a property as stock-in-trade is relevant, it does not, by itself, determine the tax head under which its rental income must be assessed.In its order, ITAT Surat ruled in favour of the landlord on the classification of his rental income, holding that the Rs 2.73 crore received from industrial buildings held as stock-in-trade was taxable under the head “Income from House Property” and not “Income from Business or Profession”.The tribunal directed the Assessing Officer to recompute his income under the house-property head, allow deductions admissible under the Income Tax Act and grant consequential relief in accordance with the law.It also directed the AO to ensure that expenses were not deducted twice under different heads of income.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Asia’s markets dive as return of Nvidia’s Huang fails to quell AI doubts
articles.summary: Markets fall in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong in latest tech-led sell-off.
articles.body:
Asian stock markets have fallen sharply as doubts continue to swirl over the AI boom, reversing a rally led by Jensen Huang’s return as CEO of Nvidia.

South Korea’s stock market led the sell-off, with the Kospi plunging 6.2 percent.

Taiwan’s Taiex closed down 4.8 percent, after earlier falling more than 8 percent.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8 percent, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index shed morning gains to finish 1.1 percent in the red.

Tech stocks linked to the AI trade suffered some of the steepest losses.

In Japan, semiconductor equipment makers Tokyo Electron and Advantest dived 12.5 percent and 12.9 percent, respectively.

South Korea’s Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the top two global memory chip makers, sank 9.9 percent and 11.1 percent, respectively.

In Taiwan, Apple supplier Hon Hai Precision Industry, also known as Foxconn, slid 8.8 percent, while top contract chip maker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) closed down 3.6 percent.

The retreat comes after Asian markets surged on Tuesday following Huang’s surprise reinstatement at the helm of chip giant Nvidia after an intervention by US President Donald Trump.

Nvidia’s reappointment of Huang, who resigned amid claims he was romantically involved with a woman suspected of working with Chinese intelligence, sent the chip giant’s New York-listed shares 31.5 percent higher on Monday, the largest single-day gain in US stock market history.

Wall Street saw modest losses on Tuesday after the previous session’s buying spree, with the S&P 500 falling 0.5 percent and the Nasdaq composite down 1.5 percent.

Markets have seen wild swings over the past month amid the Nvidia scandal and expectations that Democrats in Washington, DC, will push for greater regulation of AI following their sweeping victories in the US midterm elections.

Those headwinds have added to existing concerns that tech firms may not be able to sustain their multitrillion-dollar investments underpinning the AI boom.

Big Tech’s debt-fuelled splurge has stirred intense debate about whether it is investing in a future gold mine or a massive stock market bubble.

Global AI-related investment is forecast to reach $2.7 trillion this year and $3.6 trillion in 2027, according to technology insights company Gartner.

articles.title: InMobi ramps up hiring, senior hires ahead of IPO
articles.summary: InMobi ramps up hiring ahead of IPO, adding 200-250 AI/ML and engineering roles and senior leaders from Google, Swiggy, Amazon and Microsoft; valued at $6B.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Ahead of a potential IPO, adtech platform InMobi is stepping up its talent acquisition, adding around 200-250 employees across artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science and related engineering roles in recent months, while bringing in senior executives from companies such as Google, Swiggy, Amazon and Microsoft. The company, which has raised around $300 million, is valued at approximately $6 billion.The hiring spans campus and lateral recruitment, with a significant push at the IITs. InMobi is understood to have recruited around 150 graduates from leading IITs through the 2025 campus placement season.Separately, the group has made more than 70 lateral hires this year for AI-focused roles, including in machine learning, data science and engineering, according to people familiar with the hiring.The company has also strengthened its senior technology leadership. Jairaj Sathyanarayana has joined consumer technology subsidiary Glance as head of intelligence. An alumnus of NIT Karnataka and the University of Cincinnati, he most recently led applied research and generative AI at Swiggy. He has previously worked at Amazon and Microsoft, according to his LinkedIn profile.InMobi has appointed Chid Kollengode as senior vice-president of technology. He joined from Google, where he worked on AI assistance for cloud databases, and has previously held senior technology roles at LinkedIn, Amazon, Yahoo and Nokia. Pavan Kumar J V has joined as vice-president of engineering, having previously worked at Microsoft. Aman Gupta has returned to InMobi for a second stint as principal engineer, leading its AI and Exchange business. An IIT Delhi alumnus, Gupta previously worked on generative AI at MasterClass.In another senior appointment, InMobi recently named Hema Namburi as group chief financial officer. Namburi, who has been associated with the company for over 14 years across two stints, served as its global financial controller from 2018. She brings nearly two decades of experience across finance, audit, taxation and regulatory compliance.The group, which houses InMobi Advertising and Glance, has around 1,800-2,000 employees.When TOI reached out to InMobi, the company said: “As a matter of corporate policy, we do not comment on IPO-related speculations. Regarding the appointment of senior leaders, this is intended to cater to the growing demands of the business and its growth plans.”AI is becoming central to both businesses. InMobi has long used machine learning for audience targeting, campaign optimisation and programmatic advertising, and is expanding generative AI applications in advertising creative and personalisation. These tools allow marketers to create and tailor multiple versions of advertisements faster and at greater scale.Glance, meanwhile, is investing in visual AI, recommendation systems and personalised experiences as it builds AI-led and agentic shopping capabilities, aiming to change how consumers discover and purchase products online.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Jensen Huang says he’s thankful for second chance at Nvidia employee meeting
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around.
articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around. No company has impacted the world as deeply or profoundly as Nvidia, Huang said, according to an Nvidia employee who attended the meeting. Huang called the company’s story the most interesting in the world. According to the individual, Huang expressed contrition for his past behavior and was adamant that employees should follow the company’s code of conduct. The AI hardware leader resigned from the company on Nov. 12 amid mounting scrutiny about alleged romantic relationships with subordinates and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singaporean cloud computing company Megaspeed. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. He also said that he has been regularly attending therapy and that he had been deeply embarrassed about recent events, the source said. The CEO was met with an overwhelmingly positive reception, even receiving a standing ovation, according to the source. Huang’s return marked a nearly unprecedented case of corporate whiplash. After a wave of reports emerged stating that Huang had been involved in extramarital relationships — potentially with someone accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset — Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife in a letter sent to Nvidia employees and shared online on Nov. 8. “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” Huang wrote at the time. “I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.” Huang issued a personal statement on Nov. 17, expressing remorse but professing his admiration for and dedication to Nvidia. Huang founded the semiconductor designer in 1993 and grew it into what was once the world’s most valuable company. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” Huang wrote in that statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Less than a week later, Nvidia’s board announced that Huang would return to the company — backed by “input from senior levels of the United States government” that essentially guaranteed “Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Huang said in Tuesday’s meeting that President Donald Trump supported the company. “President Trump really, really loves our company,” Huang said, according to the Nvidia employee. Huang said that Nvidia was an apolitical company. Huang added that he returned as CEO because the board — and not the government — had wanted him to be reinstalled. The meeting, which kicked off around 9:30 a.m., lasted around an hour, according to the source, who added that Huang exited to the Foo Fighters’ song “Times Like These.”

articles.title: Americans to spend nearly $1 billion more on gas this Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Americans hitting the road this Thanksgiving Day weekend will have to navigate not just bad weather but a constant reminder of the Iran war: elevated pump prices.
articles.body: Americans hitting the road this Thanksgiving Day weekend will have to navigate not just bad weather but a constant reminder of the Iran war: elevated pump prices. Across the five-day holiday travel period that starts Wednesday, motorists are expected to spend about $980 million more on gas than last Thanksgiving, according to GasBuddy estimates shared with CNN. This Thanksgiving will challenge the Biden-era record as the most expensive Thanksgiving ever for gasoline. The AAA national average for regular gas dipped to $3.62 a gallon on Tuesday. That’s up sharply from the 2025 Thanksgiving Day price of $3.03 a gallon and narrowly above the Thanksgiving record of $3.59 set four years ago after Russia invaded Ukraine. The silver lining, however, is that gas prices have plunged in recent weeks. The national average for regular gas has plunged by 56 cents through the first 24 days of November, the most on record, according to a CNN review of AAA data. “Nobody should be busting out the champagne,” said Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy’s head of petroleum analysis. “Every state is still spending more on gas than last year – even the ones that suspended the gas tax.” Unusually high gas prices may be giving some Americans pause about traveling this Thanksgiving. AAA expects that 72.9 million people will travel by car this holiday weekend, down slightly from 73.1 million last year. “This year’s projected decrease of 200,000 travelers is due in part to this season’s record high gas prices,” AAA said in a statement, noting that August, September and October all set new monthly records at the gas pump. ‘Feeling relief’ Even though Thanksgiving Day gas prices will challenge all-time highs, the White House is taking a victory lap for the recent plunge. “Just as President Donald J. Trump predicted, gas prices are tumbling down – and American families are feeling relief just in time for Thanksgiving,” the White House said in a statement on Tuesday. It’s certainly true that there is relief relative to a few months ago. In fact, GasBuddy estimates Americans are saving $1.3 billion on fuel compared with a month ago. The recent drop in gas prices has been driven by a few factors: The Iran wild card But it’s also true that fuel prices are very high for this time of the year. Americans have paid an extra $165 billion for gas and diesel since the Iran war started in late February, according to estimates from Brown University. That equates to nearly $1,300 per household. The big X-factor for what happens next remains the Iran conflict. Energy traders were bracing for a return to full-scale hostilities after the midterm election, but that has not happened, at least not yet. However, JPMorgan Chase told clients on Tuesday that a military escalation is the No. 1 post-midterm election risk to monitor. The Wall Street bank warned that such an escalation could come as soon as next month, “prompting a spike in oil prices.” JPMorgan said the potential oil spike would likely be fleeting as long as the escalation is brief and does not involve ground troops.

articles.title: Nitin Gadkari launched India’s first barrier-free tolling in May 2026; now NHAI’s net revenue from the system has risen by 19.84% to Rs 539 crore across seven plazas in just six months
articles.summary: In what is being seen as a major boost from barrier-free tolling use, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has recorded a 19.84% rise in net
articles.body: In what is being seen as a major boost from barrier-free tolling use, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has recorded a 19.84% rise in net toll collections to Rs 538.95 crore between May and October 2026 through the system.The barrier-free Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) tolling system is functional across seven operational fee plazas.The government is introducing Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) technology across national highways as part of its move towards barrier-free toll collection.The system is being viewed as the next stage in the evolution of FASTag. Although FASTag has enabled digital toll payments, motorists still have to reduce their speed and pass through designated toll lanes and physical barriers.Barrier-free tolling launched this yearOn May 1, 2026, Road Transport and Highways minister Nitin Gadkari launched the country’s first barrier-free tolling system at the Choryasi Fee Plaza in Gujarat.It was subsequently rolled out at Mundka, Daulatpura, Gharaunda, Manoharpura, Shahjahanpur and Paranur. The Nemili and Chenasamudram fee plazas began operating under the system in November 2026.Excluding Nemili and Chenasamudram, the operational plazas collectively generated net toll revenue of Rs 538.95 crore, compared with Rs 449.72 crore during the corresponding pre-MLFF period in 2025."As on October 31, 2026, the cumulative performance across these seven plazas indicates an increase of 19.84 per cent in net revenue to NHAI, compared to the corresponding pre-MLFF baseline. Transaction volumes have also registered significant growth," NHAI said in a statement.The state-owned authority said the shift to barrier-free toll collection has delivered considerable operational and financial benefits. However, it has also encountered cases in which vehicle owners deliberately obscure, cover or tamper with their registration number plates to avoid paying tolls."NHAI has taken serious cognizance of such instances and is closely coordinating with the concerned state governments and enforcement agencies to ensure strict action against such defaulters," NHAI said.The statement said police check posts have been set up at select MLFF locations, including Gharaunda Fee Plaza. Vehicles caught engaging in such practices are being stopped and issued challans under the applicable provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.NHAI is also introducing technology-based measures powered by artificial intelligence to identify these vehicles and trace their registered owners. These include Vehicle Fingerprinting and integration with the VAHAN database, the authority said.It added that electronic notices are being issued to recover unpaid user fees. Where the dues remain unpaid despite these notices, access to applicable VAHAN services is being restricted in line with the prescribed enforcement framework.Understanding barrier-free tollingUnder barrier-free tolling, vehicles are able to continue travelling at normal highway speeds as cameras and FASTag technology identify them and deduct the applicable toll automatically.FASTag has become central to India's electronic toll collection system. FASTag is also serving as the payment mechanism for India's transition to barrier-free tolling.The technology combines Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), AI-based analytics and FASTag-enabled electronic toll collection to replace the physical barriers that currently require vehicles to slow down at toll plazas.With this arrangement, tolls can be collected without motorists having to stop, reduce speed or remain in a designated lane. Once a vehicle crosses a specified point, the system identifies it, automatically deducts the toll from its FASTag account and sends a notification to the user.Money habits form by age 7. articles.summary: Más barato que el martes
articles.body: En el tercer día de la semana, el precio medio de la electricidad se abarata de forma muy notable, con una bajada de 99,26 euros respecto al día anterior, según datos del Operador del Mercado Ibérico de la Energía (OMIE). Mañana, el precio medio de la electricidad se sitúa en 110,87 €/MWh, lo que representa un descenso del 47,24 % en comparación con el martes, que cerró en 210,13 €/MWh. Este miércoles, los consumidores deben estar atentos a las horas más caras y más baratas para gestionar mejor su consumo eléctrico. Los momentos más caros para consumir electricidad se concentran en la tarde y la noche. Desde las 17:00 los precios se disparan y se mantiene un bloque continuo hasta las 23:00, con valores por encima de los 200 €/MWh entre las 18:00 y las 23:00. El pico del día se registra entre las 20:00 y las 21:00, con 233,58 €/MWh, seguido de las 21:00 (227,52 €/MWh) y las 19:00 (215,93 €/MWh). Por la mañana hay un repunte menor entre las 07:00 y las 09:00, con un máximo de 170,92 €/MWh a las 08:00. La luz es más barata en las horas centrales del día, una excelente oportunidad de ahorro. La franja más económica va de las 11:00 a las 14:00, con 5,83 €/MWh cada hora, y las 14:00-15:00 también se mantienen muy bajas (7,35 €/MWh). También hay precios reducidos en la madrugada, entre las 02:00 y las 06:00, con valores en torno a los 61-63 €/MWh. En total, 13 horas del día quedan por debajo de la media. En el análisis de las franjas horarias del miércoles, destaca una enorme diferencia entre la hora más cara y la más barata, que alcanza los 227,75 €/MWh, lo que subraya la importancia de planificar el consumo eléctrico para maximizar el ahorro. Esta volatilidad sugiere que trasladar el uso de electrodomésticos al mediodía puede suponer un gran beneficio económico para los consumidores.

articles.title: Egg prices fall as much as 20% in just 8-10 days as bird flu stalls exports from Tamil Nadu, which accounts for over 90% of India’s egg exports; but farmers face 30%-50% higher feed costs
articles.summary: Egg prices have plunged in the last few days after a bird flu outbreak in Tamil Nadu has disrupted exports.
articles.body: Egg prices have plunged in the last few days after a bird flu outbreak in Tamil Nadu has disrupted exports. Egg prices have crashed anywhere between 10%-20% over the past 8-10 days.The surplus supplies are being directed into the domestic market at a time when seasonal demand is already losing momentum in southern India.Farm-gate prices, which had climbed following Chhath Puja, have now begun falling, upsetting poultry farmers who had anticipated better returns during the winter months.Egg prices crash and demand fallsConsumption demand in southern states has also weakened during the Hindu month of Karthik, adding to the excess supply in the market.The price drop has come even as production expenses remain high, according to an ET report. Maize and soybean, two key ingredients used in poultry feed, have become 30%-50% more expensive than a year ago, putting further pressure on farmers’ margins.Poultry feed primarily comprises ingredients such as maize, broken rice, soybean meal and millets. Maize prices have risen by around 50% over the past year, while soybean meal has become approximately 30% more expensive.Soybean meal is a by-product obtained when soybean seeds are crushed to extract oil. Poultry industry players and farmers had been counting on higher realisations during winter, when egg and chicken consumption typically increases across India.Egg prices had begun moving upwards across the country after Chhath Puja, reaching a peak of Rs 6.70 per egg in Namakkal, India’s poultry hub, on November 11. However, the upward trend quickly reversed after bird flu was confirmed in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, on November 13. The outbreak prompted containment measures, including the culling of birds and a 90-day prohibition on raising poultry in the affected area.In Namakkal, egg prices fell to Rs 5.60 apiece, marking a decline of around 19%. The fall has been relatively modest in Delhi, West Bengal, Gujarat and Maharashtra, where prices have dropped by about 6%-10%, while most southern states have recorded declines exceeding 15%.“Namakkal in Tamil Nadu is India’s egg export hub and accounts for over 90% of the country’s egg exports. The region was exporting about one crore eggs per day last year during the same time, which had reduced to about 15-20 eggs per day just before the outbreak,” Sanjeev Chintawar, chief operating officer, National Egg Coordination Committee told the financial daily.The seasonal dip in demand has compounded the oversupply in southern India, as consumption of non-vegetarian food is restricted during Karthik, a month in the Indian calendar. “Farmers had reduced production for two months before Diwali to cope with the higher feed costs and planned to increase production in winter hoping to get better realisation,” said Chintawar.He added, “With feed suppliers refusing to sell feed on credit to the poultry farmers due to supressed prices of eggs and chicken, bird nutrition has been adversely affected either knowingly or unknowingly.”The price squeeze is also hurting poultry farmers producing chicken. “Farmers are bleeding. The production cost of chicken is over 120/kg, while farmers are getting just about 80/kg,” said KG Anand, general manager, Venkateshwara Hatcheries, the largest fully integrated poultry conglomerate of India.The wider feed industry is also struggling amid the downturn. “Everyone is making losses. We have no clue how to survive this situation,” said Divya Kumar Gulati, immediate past president, Compound Livestock Feed Manufacturers Association of India, the industry body representing the animal feed industry.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Nvidia is crucial to the economy. An AI wipeout could unleash unexpected consequences
articles.summary: In the two weeks without Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia, Wall Street turned its back on AI. A deep and prolonged stock market sell-off exposed risks to an economy that is increasingly reliant on AI and the wealth it has generated.
articles.body: In the two weeks without Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia, Wall Street turned its back on AI. A deep and prolonged stock market sell-off exposed risks to an economy that is increasingly reliant on AI and the wealth it has generated. The stock market was up more than 14% just over a month ago but ended last week on the verge of turning negative for the year — a rapid reversal fueled by concerns about the sustainability of the AI business. That alarmed President Donald Trump, leading him to help orchestrate Huang’s return, which he believed would catalyze a stock market rebound. Trump was proven correct – for one day, at least. The stock market plunge had threatened to take down the economy with it, and the Trump administration grew to believe Huang was too big to fire. Nvidia’s 28% stock plunge in the days following Huang’s resignation spread throughout the broader industry. That posed a problem because of the ultra concentration at the top of the stock market: The five biggest AI companies on the S&P 500 – Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta – combine for an astonishing 25% of the overall market’s value. As confidence in AI eroded, it brought the entire stock market into a correction. So Trump may be right, although not for the reasons you might think: A sustained market decline wouldn’t necessarily threaten the expected trillions of dollars pouring in from AI investment. Instead, it could erode confidence among the consumers who have kept spending through it all: America’s wealthy. The K-shaped economy Rising prices have taken significant bites out of middle- and low-income Americans’ paychecks over the past several months, and high mortgage rates and home prices have kept many out of the housing market. But if American consumers were worried about inflation this year, you’d be hard pressed to find it in broad economic data — particularly consumer spending, which represents more than two-thirds of US economic output. Consumer spending in the third quarter clocked in at a robust 3.8% annualized pace, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis. In August, inflation-adjusted consumer spending rose by the highest amount in a year. But look a bit closer, and it becomes apparent that a select few are shouldering the brunt of the work this year. The top 40% of earners spent $15.7 trillion through September, according to economists at RSM US. The middle- and low-income Americans spent only $6.7 trillion. That means the wealthiest Americans accounted for 70% of all consumer spending this year, up from 61% last year. Some economists call that phenomenon a K-shaped economy, a widening wealth gap between America’s highest and lowest earners. The K-shape is hotly debated and is an inexact science. Some economic measures show a narrowing K, depending on the perspective and timeframe. But the trend in recent years has been clear: The wealthy have been outspending the bulk of Americans who have become somewhat more frugal. That’s not only because they’re richer; it’s because of what kind of wealth they hold. The top 20% of earners own more than half of America’s overall home value; just 3% of America’s home value is owned by the bottom 20% of earners, according to the New York Federal Reserve. Another contributing factor: Wealthy Americans are significantly more invested in the stock market. The top 20% of earners control 87% of the wealth generated by America’s individually owned stocks, according to the Federal Reserve’s Distributional Financial Accounts. Because stock market holdings are so concentrated among wealthy households, so too is the spending it generates: Three-quarters of spending created by the market flows through the top 20% of earners, according to RSM US. So, with a large portion of their wealth tied up in real estate and the stock market, America’s wealthiest have largely ignored this year’s inflationary pressures and kept on spending. But if the market rally ends, the spending engine — and the economic growth it generated — could sputter. Next stop: Recession? If consumer spending is the economy’s engine, AI has been the fuel over the past couple of years. The technology’s rapid expansion has supported the stock market rally: The 10 most valuable public companies are all tech-focused and make up roughly 40% of the value of the S&P 500. But investment in AI has also supported the economy. A quarter of this year’s economic growth has come from the AI infrastructure buildout, according to ING. That investment probably isn’t going to dry up anytime soon. The industry is expected to spend $1.1 trillion on AI infrastructure this year and $1.8 trillion next year, according to a Goldman Sachs forecast from earlier this month. Investors haven’t lost confidence in AI’s potential as a transformative technology, noted Keith Lerner, chief market strategist at Truist Wealth. Instead, they’ve lost confidence that AI companies’ spending will turn into sustainable profits anytime soon. Recent events haven’t helped. Neocloud CoreWeave sounded alarm bells about the AI business in October, when its bond yields surged to 15%, making its borrowing costs nearly twice its return on investment. Democrats’ sweeping victory in the midterm elections included many who called for increased regulation of AI and moratoriums on data center construction. And the Nvidia scandal had (temporarily) cost the industry its de facto central banker and renewed calls for increased scrutiny of US AI chip exports. But a slowdown in AI investment alone wouldn’t lead to a recession, said Joe Brusuelas, chief economist at RSM US. “That scenario would also require a financial market event,” he said. In other words: A sustained decline in AI stocks could lead to a recession. “Rising equities are far more important to the sustainability of the expansion,” he said. Reasons for hope Considering the market hit a record high on October 6, any discussion about a potential recession may seem jarring. But the Nasdaq remains 14% below its all-time high despite a massive 6% rally on Monday. The broader S&P 500 is more than 8% below its peak. Despite the market enduring such a roller coaster ride in a short period of time, there may be reasons for hope. For one, the wipeout sent Big Tech valuations through the floor, creating some pretty cheap-looking stocks. The S&P 500 tech sector’s price-to-earnings ratio — a measure of a stock’s relative value — has fallen 45% this year to around 15, below its pandemic-era nadir, noted Lerner. The rapid decline in price-to-earnings value has only two historic parallels: the dot-com bust and the global financial crisis. “There are significant uncertainties around AI, but it is difficult to argue that the current backdrop is more uncertain than the early stages of the pandemic,” he said. Another reason for optimism: In similar market declines over a single month, the average rebound from the market bottom has been around 20% — a rapid snapback that can undo significant damage from the decline. That’s why analysts at Goldman Sachs forecast positive returns for stocks next year — noting, however, “the path could be bumpy.” Still, that’s no guarantee the market will bounce all the way back anytime soon. It may continue to slide and take wealthy Americans’ spending down with it.

articles.title: Anthropic stock sinks further below IPO price as investors sour on the Amodei AI bet
articles.summary: Anthropic loses more ground after its sizzling IPO.
articles.body:
Welcome to the public markets, Anthropic ( ANT ).

Less than a week after its blockbuster IPO, Anthropic shares look to be settling further below their $83 offering price. After a 6.5% drubbing to $81.91 by Tuesday's close, the stock fell a further 5.7% in premarket trading on Wednesday to $77.22, on renewed fears over the health of the AI trade.

Anthropic's stock opened on IPO day at $111.50, briefly topped $115 and carried a valuation north of $2 trillion. Now the stock is down more than 30% from its highs and the market cap stands at about $1.09 trillion.

This isn't necessarily a referendum on Anthropic's technology. It's a referendum on the price investors are being asked to pay for it. At roughly 30 times trailing sales, the valuation leaves very little room for disappointment.

Wall Street is also questioning the enormous cost of building AI infrastructure, whether data-center spending can keep accelerating and how quickly these companies can turn their technology into sustainable profits.

There's another uncomfortable wrinkle for Anthropic as well.

CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei each disclosed selling roughly $280 million in shares as part of the IPO. Those sales were made to underwriters at the offering price and aren't evidence of some sudden executive exodus.

But the optics won't help investor confidence against a risk-off backdrop for AI stocks.

articles.title: From construction equipment to postal services: Cabinet clears Rs 19,934 crore package; key decisions
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a series of proposals involving a combined outlay of nearly Rs 19,934 crore, including an Rs 11,000-crore scheme
articles.body: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a series of proposals involving a combined outlay of nearly Rs 19,934 crore, including an Rs 11,000-crore scheme to strengthen India's construction and infrastructure equipment manufacturing ecosystem, a new container terminal in Tamil Nadu and a greenfield airport in Assam.The decisions were announced by Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw at a press briefing following the Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The Cabinet also approved the continuation of two schemes for the Department of Posts during the 16th Finance Commission period, from 2026-27 to 2030-31, with a combined outlay of Rs 2,632 crore.Here are the key decisions announced at the briefing:Rs 11,000 crore scheme to boost construction equipment manufacturingThe Cabinet approved the Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem with a financial outlay of Rs 11,000 crore.The scheme, to be implemented by the ministry of heavy industries over eight years from 2026-27, aims to promote domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment and components. It also provides for setting up a dedicated testing facility in the country.According to the government, India's construction and infrastructure equipment industry was the world's third largest, after China and the US, with a market size of around Rs 97,500 crore in 2024-25. It is projected to more than double to around Rs 2.28 lakh crore by 2029-30.The scheme will have two components: sales-linked incentives for eligible original equipment manufacturers and component makers, with rates ranging from 13% to 8% of incremental sales over five years; and a grant of up to Rs 375 crore for setting up a dedicated testing facility.The government said the initiative would support domestic production of equipment such as ship-to-shore cranes, tunnel boring machines, hydraulic excavators and off-highway trucks.New container terminal at Kamarajar PortThe Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the development of a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port in Tamil Nadu at an estimated project cost of Rs 4,288.26 crore, including GST.The project will be developed under the public-private partnership model on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer basis. It will involve construction of a 900-metre-long terminal with an annual handling capacity of two million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs).The project will be implemented in two phases. The first phase will have a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs, while the second will add 0.9 million TEUs. The terminal will have a design draft of 18 metres and will be capable of handling large container vessels, including ships with a capacity of up to 24,346 TEUs.The concessionaire will arrange the investment for the terminal, while Kamarajar Port Limited will separately bear an estimated Rs 450 crore towards dredging. The concession period will be 40 years, including a construction period of 48 months.The government said the additional capacity would help meet rising containerised export-import demand from the Chennai-Ennore industrial region and the wider southern hinterland. The project is expected to generate around 750 direct and indirect jobs during construction and increase employment by about 800 people during operations.Greenfield airport approved for Doloo in AssamThe Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs also approved a greenfield airport at Doloo in Assam's Cachar district, near Silchar, at an estimated cost of Rs 2,014 crore.The Airports Authority of India will develop the airport to address the operational and space constraints of the existing civil enclave at Silchar Airport, which is located on defence land, and accommodate rising passenger traffic.The proposed terminal will cover 12,351 square metres and will be able to handle 800 passengers during peak hours. The project also includes a 2,705-metre-long runway, designed for A-320 aircraft operations, and an apron with parking capacity for six A-320 aircraft, along with a dedicated isolation bay.The government said the airport would improve air connectivity for South Assam and adjoining areas of neighbouring states, while supporting trade, tourism and economic activity in the Barak Valley.Postal Operations Scheme gets Rs 1,141 croreThe Cabinet approved the continuation of the Postal Operations Scheme with an outlay of Rs 1,141 crore for the five-year period from 2026-27 to 2030-31.The scheme aims to modernise India Post's network, improve mail and parcel operations, strengthen last-mile delivery and expand citizen-centric services, particularly in rural and underserved areas.It includes six components covering rural access to the postal network, mail and parcel network optimisation, international mail infrastructure, marketing and service quality, and philately operations.The largest allocation of Rs 575 crore is for mail network optimisation, including modernisation of mail handling, delivery systems and transport networks. Parcel network optimisation has been allocated Rs 278 crore, while Rs 120 crore will go towards improving rural access and postal infrastructure.Other allocations include Rs 100 crore for marketing and service quality, Rs 60 crore for philately operations and Rs 8 crore for international mail infrastructure.India Post operates a network of 1.65 lakh post offices, including nearly 1.5 lakh in rural areas. The government said the scheme would support its expanding role in parcel delivery, e-commerce logistics, financial inclusion and digital services.Rs 1,491 crore for modernising postal infrastructureThe Cabinet also approved the continuation of the Estates Management Scheme for the Department of Posts, with an outlay of Rs 1,491 crore over five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31.The scheme aims to modernise post office buildings and residential colonies through new construction, reconstruction, renovation and uniform branding. It also includes the restoration of heritage postal buildings.Under the plan, Rs 280 crore has been earmarked to construct 190 departmental postal buildings on vacant land, while Rs 108 crore will be used to rebuild 50 dilapidated structures. Another Rs 318 crore will go towards renovating and branding 2,550 departmental sub-post offices.The scheme also provides Rs 37.5 crore to upgrade 2,500 post offices operating from rented premises and Rs 180 crore to restore 20 heritage postal buildings. A further Rs 357.5 crore has been allocated for renovating 150 postal residential colonies.The remaining provisions include Rs 100 crore for sustainable and accessibility-related facilities, such as solar power, rainwater harvesting, ramps and Braille signage, and Rs 100 crore for an integrated technology centre in Bengaluru to support postal technology services.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Dell stock tanks after blowout earnings. Wall Street Just Isn't Impressed.
articles.summary: Dell's stock takes it on the chin despite a blowout quarter.
articles.body:
Wall Street isn't getting Dell's ( DELL ) quarter today, and it's bizarre.

The computer giant-turned-AI server play checked every single box a bull on the AI trade would want when it reported earnings late Tuesday.

Revenue of $54.9 billion. Wall Street was looking for $49.33 billion. Adjusted earnings of $9.45 a share against estimates of $6.57. That's not a beat. That's a demolition .

The company raised its full-year revenue outlook to $202 billion, well above Wall Street's roughly $195 billion forecast. Its earnings guidance also came in ahead of expectations, with adjusted EPS projected at $29.68. Meanwhile, Dell's AI backlog has ballooned to $132.3 billion.

This isn't the first time this year that Dell has paired a big earnings report with a raised outlook.

The response: the stock is down 6% in premarket trading on Wednesday. It tanked 11.83% on Tuesday as it got caught up in a risk-off backdrop for AI stocks. Shares have been torched, falling 36% in the past month.

But Dell's quarter is what the AI infrastructure boom is supposed to look like. Customers are buying. Orders are stacking up. Dell is shipping the equipment powering the AI buildout. And management keeps coming back to Wall Street with bigger numbers.

That is the bizarre part of this earnings story.

Dell shares were already under pressure heading into the report. Now the company has delivered another monster quarter, raised its outlook and shown investors a massive pipeline of AI demand. Yet the market is still finding reasons to sell.

"Dell's strong AI order backlog and upbeat revenue outlook demonstrate AI demand," JP Morgan analyst Albert Hung said.

At some point, investors need to explain what exactly they want from this company.

The AI trade has plenty of companies promising a revolution. Dell is showing up with the orders, the revenue and the backlog.

If this isn't good enough for Wall Street, what is? The fact it isn't say a alot about the health of the AI trade at the moment.

articles.title: Elderly man sells property to son-in-law and faces Rs 20.94 lakh tax penalty for alleged cash transaction; ITAT finds no proof of cash receipt and cancels penalty, also deletes additions over farm income and loan
articles.summary: An elderly taxpayer faced a penalty of Rs 20.94 lakh after the Income Tax Department concluded that he had received this amount in cash while selling a
articles.body: An elderly taxpayer faced a penalty of Rs 20.94 lakh after the Income Tax Department concluded that he had received this amount in cash while selling a property to his son-in-law, in contravention of the Income Tax Act.The Income Tax Department did not accept his explanation at the first appellate stage and sustained the penalty. Read on to know why the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) gave relief.What the case is aboutThe dispute centred on the sale of an immovable property. The AO concluded that the taxpayer had received Rs 20.94 lakh in cash in connection with the transfer, thereby breaching Section 269SS of the Income Tax Act.A penalty equivalent to the disputed amount was then imposed under Section 271D. The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), or CIT(A), also subsequently upheld the penalty.The property seller then challenged the department's finding that any cash had changed hands.The taxpayer explained that, being elderly, he had decided to sell his property to his son-in-law for an agreed consideration of Rs 45.50 lakh. The sale deed was executed on August 12, 2015, when the property's stamp duty value stood at Rs 66.44 lakh.The taxpayer contended that the advocate drafting the sale deed had entered the difference of Rs 20.94 lakh as cash received solely to make the consideration recorded in the document correspond with the property's stamp duty value. He maintained throughout that he had not actually received this sum in cash.Challenging the penalty before the ITAT, the taxpayer argued that the department had incorrectly treated the amount recorded in the sale deed as proof of an actual cash receipt.The tax department also raised questions about certain deposits, which the taxpayer attributed to his agricultural activities and a loan.Why did ITAT Hyderabad rule in favour of property seller?On October 9, 2026, the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Hyderabad, ruled in the elderly man’s favour, cancelling the penalty and granting relief in respect of these additions.The ITAT deleted the Rs 20.94 lakh penalty because the taxpayer consistently denied receiving the cash, and his son-in-law supported this claim through an affidavit stating that no cash had been paid.Although the sale deed recorded the amount as received, the Assessing Officer had not examined the son-in-law to verify the alleged payment. The tribunal considered these facts along with the explanation that the amount had been included to match the stamp duty value and the family circumstances surrounding the property transfer.It concluded that the taxpayer had established reasonable cause under Section 273B of the Income Tax Act, which provides relief from penalties in such circumstances, and directed the penalty to be deleted.“The man pointed out that the Assessing Officer had not examined the son-inlaw or independently verified whether the payment had actually taken place,” Advocate K Sai Teja, practising in the Supreme Court of India told ET.In view of these circumstances, the Tribunal found reasonable cause for the alleged breach under Section 273B and ordered the Income Tax Department to remove the entire penalty of Rs 20.94 lakh, he adds.The tribunal's decision did not amount to a conclusive finding that no cash had changed hands simply because the taxpayer denied receiving the money. It recognised that the statement recorded in a registered sale deed constituted relevant evidence and could not be rejected merely on the basis of a later denial.ITAT also removed tax additions linked to agricultural income and a loanIn a separate appeal relating to the same assessment year, the taxpayer contested additions made by the Income Tax Department during reassessment proceedings. The AO had identified cash deposits of Rs 48.60 lakh in the taxpayer's bank account, along with time deposits totalling Rs 13 lakh. Since the taxpayer had not filed an income tax return for assessment year 2016-17, the AO completed the reassessment on March 21, 2024, assessing his total income at Rs 87.48 lakh.Among the adjustments made, the AO classified certain amounts claimed to be agricultural income and a loan as unexplained money under Section 69A of the Income Tax Act.The taxpayer maintained that he owned 4.86 acres of agricultural land, which he had leased to two individuals for cultivation. The land was used to grow sunflower seeds, and the cultivators transferred his one-third share of the proceeds from the sale of the produce through banking channels. The two receipts under dispute amounted to Rs 1.38 lakh and Rs 1.20 lakh.Arguing against the additions, the taxpayer said the money represented his share of the agricultural produce and, therefore, could not be classified as unexplained. The ITAT observed that the ownership of the agricultural land, the cultivation activities and the receipt of the disputed amounts through banking channels were not in question.Since the tax department had not furnished evidence to disprove the taxpayer's explanation, the tribunal directed the AO to remove both additions. The amounts deleted were Rs 1,38,000 and Rs 1,20,250, respectively.The tribunal also granted relief on another addition of Rs 3 lakh, which the taxpayer said he had borrowed from an individual. In support of his explanation, he furnished a bank statement and a confirmation from the lender.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Oil edges down as supply glut prospect offsets Middle East disruption fears
articles.summary: By Anna Hirtenstein LONDON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oi...
articles.body:
LONDON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East.

Brent crude futures declined ‌44 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.96 a barrel at 1035 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped ‌62 cents, or 0.8%, to $81.43 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained more than 2% on Tuesday.

"Investors are preoccupied with the thought of supply exceeding demand," ​said Tamas Varga, an oil analyst at PVM, a brokerage.

On Wednesday, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh's financial district. Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, is part of a complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast that also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude.

A build-up in crude inventories is also contributing to ‌the softer oil prices, Varga said.

US crude ⁠stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended November 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. [API/S]

Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude ⁠inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average.

"Uncertainty about OPEC's 2027 policies in the upcoming November 29 meeting, especially with the UAE no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies and Iraq seeking higher oil output capacity, as well as broader market risk-off are ​some ​reasons," said Zhenqiang Seto, a senior research specialist for oil at ​LSEG.

OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings ‌on November 29 to decide on their 2027 output policy.

"Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will be determined at the OPEC+ meeting, Ueno said.

Iraq is pressing OPEC+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity, four people familiar with the matter said, heightening ‌tensions over a review that will help determine how much members ​can pump next year.

Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has also reopened after ​an "unlawful group" closed a valve on the pipeline, with ​oil beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya.

"However, attacks on ‌ships near the Strait of Hormuz and exchanges ​of attacks between Saudi Arabia and ​the Houthis have raised uncertainty over the sustainability of this trend," Ueno said.

A container ship was targeted and came to a stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards ​said, according to state media.

articles.body: Onions are a staple food in Indian households, but their ability to make you cry can stretch beyond your kitchens! In fact, until some years ago any major rise in onion prices used to be an important election issue.Onion prices have been rising steadily this year, and for the last two months have been the item with the highest inflation. According to government data, retail prices of 41 out of 42 essential commodities have risen over the year. But onions stand out with their over 100% inflation rate.So why are onion prices so closely tracked? What does a rise in onion price mean for you beyond the obvious rise in your grocery and food budget?Why have onion prices been rising and what do they mean for inflation?Onion prices have risen due to supply side issues. articles.title: AI is crushing software stocks — and a debt wall looms: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: AI fears are spreading from software stocks to software loans, with a big debt wall due in 2028 and 2029.
articles.body:
Stock investors have been dumping software names this year, fearing that AI will eat their lunch. Lenders are catching up.

Software stocks held steady on Tuesday while chip stocks sank about 8%. It was a rare calm day for a group that's been pummeled in 2026 .

Salesforce ( CRM ), Adobe ( ADBE ), ServiceNow ( NOW ), HubSpot ( HUBS ), and Intuit ( INTU ) are down roughly 25% to 60% this year. The iShares software ETF ( IGV ) is down about 10%, while semiconductors as a group ( SOXX ) are still up about 28%.

Now the pain is spreading to the debt market. "Software is being hit by a double whammy of AI disruption and rates staying higher for longer," Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk wrote on Tuesday .

(Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

Software borrowers are paying up for AI risk

Yields on software leveraged loans have climbed above 13%, up from about 9% at the start of the year. These are loans to companies that already carry lots of debt, often owned by private equity firms.

Yields on leveraged loans overall are still under 10%. In January, software borrowers paid about 1 percentage point more than average. Now it's more than 3 points.

That's the price lenders are charging for AI risk.

Private equity firms loaded up on software in the easy-money years. At the 2022 peak, software was more than 30% of all buyout deal value.

Many of those deals ran on seven-year loans written in 2021 and 2022, when rates were near zero. They came with minimal amortization , meaning borrowers pay back little of the principal along the way.

That builds a maturity wall , a pile of debt due at about the same time. Software's hits in 2028 and 2029.

About $65 billion of software loans mature in those two years, by Yahoo Finance's reading of Apollo's data. About $45 billion of it is rated B- or lower, deep in junk territory.

Rolling those loans over isn't getting easier. Software's 2028 wall has shrunk just 10% this year, versus 22% for the rest of the market, Sløk wrote on Nov. 12.

Money isn't getting cheaper, either. The Fed raised rates in September, and Polymarket bettors see about a 96% chance of another hike on Dec. 9.

HubSpot co-founder Brian Halligan, back as CEO after five years away, sees AI as a boost. "HubSpot, I think ... is going to get a real tailwind from AI," he told Yahoo Finance on Tuesday.

Not everyone is convinced, including Bill Gunderson of GCG Advisory Partners, who told Yahoo Finance Tuesday that much of software has become a slow-growth trap.

articles.title: 10 big money topics you might have to tackle over turkey: A Yahoo Finance guide to Nvidia, markets, and more
articles.summary: A cheat sheet of 10 big topics to give you an edge on your family this holiday.
articles.body:
There's something about Thanksgiving and the world of finance. Family members — both alike and different — thrust together in a pressure cooker of food, football, and more food. Pressure that squeezes opinions out and volumes up.

As Bloomberg's Joe Weisenthal mused on this week , the "Thanksgiving effect" is real. Remember the bitcoin boom of 2017 that had everyone buying post-turkey? The same thing happened in 1999 with internet stocks. Maybe we'll get something this week.

We've decided to put together a little cheat sheet of 10 big topics to give you an edge on your family. Or, in the generous spirit of Thanksgiving, to "educate."

The main takeaway for the stock market these days is "wow." We have had an extremely zesty month , from the midterm elections pouring water on companies building data centers and raising hopes the Iran war will end to the Anthropic IPO to the Nvidia… drama (more on that below).

Remember: The stock market is still up over 5% for the year. Not a great return, historically, but it's still positive.

The bullish take: With stocks down (or somewhat down), this is a great buying opportunity — just look at the favorable price-to-earnings ratio the S&P 500 has! Corporate earnings are the backbone of any valuation, and companies are earning well and expect that to continue. The consumer is still strong, stocks usually do well after a period of fear, and as the TKer's Sam Ro likes to remind us, "stocks usually go up over the long term."

The bearish take: The stock market's foundation may be strong consumer spending, but its big gains are largely AI-driven. Have you seen how concentrated the S&P 500 is in just a few Big Tech companies? If the AI trade can't pay for itself, those massive investments (and degrading chips) will cause some big problems. Plus, do normal people want AI? Will they pay for it? Because at these spending rates, the math looks tough. And the Fed is going to hike rates.

Heading into the final month of the year, inflation isn't where the Fed needs it to be, and it's been going in the wrong direction. This has all but locked in a rate hike in December, and now there's chatter of a jumbo rate hike (50 basis points) possible at the next meeting or in the future. (Remember, a basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point.) Meanwhile, the labor market is in a low-hire, low-fire framework . Both unemployment and hiring are low. If you have a job, great. If you don't, ouch. Overall GDP is strong, but things are still K-shaped. Great for the haves — the top of the K — rough for the have-nots.

articles.title: Fed’s preferred inflation metric rose in October as final 2026 rate meeting nears

articles.body:
Inflation increased slightly in October , new data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) showed Wednesday, as the Federal Reserve’s final rate-setting meeting approaches in two weeks.

The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3 percent last month and was up 3.8 percent relative to October 2025, the BEA reported .

The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland projected PCE inflation , the central bank’s preferred measure of prices, would be up 0.3 percent from September and 3.8 percent compared with a year prior.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

“Another hot inflation reading for October,” Heather Long, the chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, wrote Wednesday on the social platform X. Long noted annual PCE inflation hit its highest point since May.

The consumer price index (CPI), another measure of inflation, increased 0.4 percent from September to October.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), which releases the CPI monthly, was unable to provide annual inflation data for last month because of the record-long government shutdown that took up all of October 2025 .

Annual inflation, according to the PCE, previously increased from 3.4 percent in August to 3.6 percent in September.

Annual PCE inflation in February was 2.8 percent . But the Iran war , which the U.S. and Israel launched on the final day of that month, has pushed up energy prices.

The price of gas and other energy goods rose 0.8 percent from September to October, after increasing 9.2 percent from August to September, the BEA reported .

The average price of a gallon of regular gas is roughly $3.59 as of Wednesday, according to data from AAA .

While that is about 70 cents cheaper than a month ago, as gas prices have declined in line with seasonal trends, a gallon of gas is roughly 60 cents more expensive than it was two days before the Iran conflict began.

Food and beverage prices increased 0.4 percent after holding steady for two straight months, according to the PCE. That marked the highest monthly increase since April, when food and beverage prices rose 0.5 percent.

Core prices, which exclude more volatile energy and food costs, increased 0.3 percent from September to October and were up 3.3 percent from October 2025, per the PCE. Core annual inflation was 3.1 percent in September.

The Cleveland Fed projected core PCE prices to rise 0.3 percent month over month in October and to be up 3.2 percent from a year prior.

Long wrote that core inflation “came in hotter than expected,” adding the BEA’s report is “yet another reminder that the inflation problem right now goes beyond a mere energy shock.”

Housing prices also increased 0.3 percent from September to October, tied for the second-highest monthly increase this year. Housing costs also rose 0.3 percent in March, May, July and September.

Stubborn inflation has been above the Fed’s 2 percent target for five and a half years, and the recent increase amid the war prompted central bank officials to raise interest rates by a quarter point in September.

Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) officials followed up the panel’s first rate hike since July 2023 by holding rates at a range of 3.75 percent to 4 percent in late October. But multiple FOMC officials have previewed future hikes , with the committee set to meet again Dec. 8-9.

“It is imperative that we restore inflation to our 2 percent target in a timely manner and on a sustained basis,” John Williams, the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, said Monday at the University of Mount Saint Vincent.

The BLS will release CPI data for November on Dec. 10, a day after the FOMC’s meeting concludes.

Traders as of Wednesday are pricing in a 97.8 percent chance of FOMC officials raising rates by a quarter point next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool .

While Americans are dealing with elevated prices, economic growth surged in the third quarter.

The country’s gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent from July through September, the BEA reported Wednesday.

That is 2.1 percentage points higher than the second quarter and 0.9 points higher than the bureau’s initial estimate for the third quarter. The BEA will release finalized GDP data for the third quarter on Dec. 23.

articles.title: How much of the 2027 3.6 percent Social Security COLA you’ll keep
articles.summary: Checks will rise 3.6% next year to keep up with inflation, marking the largest yearly increase since 2023.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Social Security recipients can now check exactly how much more money they’ll get each month in 2027.

The new amounts are showing in people’s online accounts this month. The Social Security Administration will also mail notices in December.

Checks will rise 3.6% next year to keep up with inflation, which reached 3.7% in September. It marks the largest yearly bump since 2023, which saw an 8.7% increase.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

The raise works out to be about $75 more a month, or $900 a year, for the average retired worker, making the average monthly check for retired workers $2,170 starting January. People who receive Supplemental Security income will see higher payments starting Dec. 31.

The raise affects about 76 million Americans, including roughly 55 million retired workers.

Most retirees won’t keep full 3.6% increase

Medicare’s premium for doctor visits and out-patient care is taken directly out of Social Security checks, and it’s going up $6.50 next year to $209.40 a month.

Most people paying the standard premium will still see increases of 3% or more. To figure out your own number, multiply your current monthly check by 3.6%, subtract $6.50, then divide that amount by your current check.

Higher earners may pay more. Medicare charges extra premiums to people whose income tops certain levels, based on tax returns from two years earlier. Going even $1 over a limit triggers the full extra charge.

Medicare’s yearly sign-up period ends Dec. 7. Some prescription drug plan premiums are rising after the Trump administration said it would end federal premium help after 2026. Research by health policy group KFF found many people who keep their current plans will see small increases or even lower premiums, but some large plans are raising prices significantly.

Next year, yearly out-of-pocket drug costs will be capped at $2,400. The highest allowed deductible will rise to $700.

articles.title: Trump Accounts surpass $1B in donations from friends, family
articles.summary: Friends and family members have poured more than $1 billion into President Trump’s investment accounts for children, the Treasury Department announced Tuesday, bringing total deposits in the program to more than $9 billion. articles.body:
Friends and family members have poured more than $1 billion into President Trump’s investment accounts for children, the Treasury Department announced Tuesday, bringing total deposits in the program to more than $9 billion.

More than 3 million people have contributed to individual Trump Accounts since the program launched earlier this year under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that was signed into law in July 2025.

“The American people are investing in Trump Accounts with a generosity that represents the finest instincts of our national character,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement .

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

“President Trump wanted to make it especially easy to contribute to Trump Accounts, and friends and families across the country are seizing that opportunity to help the next generation build wealth from day one,” he continued. “With every contribution, we are bringing the promise of long-term financial security within reach of American children from every kind of family and every kind of background.”

Bessent said Trump himself made contributions to individual accounts this week. The administration did not disclose how much the president donated or who received the money.

The tax-advantaged investment accounts are eligible for American children born during Trump’s second term in office — between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028 — and are eligible for a one-time $1,000 contribution from the federal government.

The Treasury Department has since expanded the program through automatic enrollment , opening an additional 60 million accounts for eligible children younger than 18 years with valid Social Security numbers.

Parents or legal guardians must still claim their children’s accounts before they can receive private contributions. Friends and family members can collectively contribute up to $5,000 annually, including up to $2,500 in employer contributions.

The program drew billions of dollars in philanthropic commitments, including a $6.25 billion pledge from Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and his wife, Susan Dell, to provide $250 to children living in ZIP codes with a median family income of $150,000 or less.

Trump has repeatedly touted the accounts as a means of expanding stock market participation among younger Americans, arguing earlier this year that the initiative could help curb growing support for socialism and communism.
